result.narrative:
Hessler Maschinenbau is a deteriorating buyer on first-party data. One overdue invoice of USD 640,000 is open under policy TCI-EX-2026-0001, now 52 days past due, and the pattern across successive notifications is clearly lengthening: 9 days late in March, 19 days in June, 52 now. Combined outstanding of 3.24M (640k overdue plus 2.6M not yet due) exceeds the 3.0M accepted credit limit on the single reporting policy, and all exposure sits with one insurer. A severity 4 news item dated 2026-11-08 reports the company has fallen behind with component suppliers after a large customer postponed acceptance of two production lines.

The score is 75.3, High Risk, with PD 0.775, from 0.65 x 74.0 (payment, 52 DPD) + 0.35 x 77.8 (news). The adjudicator agreed with the direction but attached caveats, and they matter here: payment weighted alone is 48.1, short of the High Risk cutoff, so the 27.2 weighted points from ILL-003 are what carry the score into the band. That article is recorded only as "Illustrative" and rests on three unnamed suppliers speaking to an unnamed regional paper, and it attributes the arrears to the same customer-acceptance delay that plausibly generated the overdue invoice — so one cash-flow event may be scored twice across two supposedly independent legs. The adjudicator also flags that the notification's owed field of 3240000.0 overstates at-risk overdue exposure, which is USD 640,000, and that the as-of date for the 52 DPD figure is ambiguous.

The recommendation is FREEZE on LIM-OS06-1 (Tamrin Exports, EXPORT, USD): current limit 3000000, revised limit 3000000, change 0, on the basis that outstanding exposure is already at or above the limit and there is nothing left to cut. Expected loss is 1674000 before and after, so the freeze stops new exposure rather than reducing what is there; PD of 0.775 remains far above the 0.25 target. Given the caveats, the sensible sequence is to apply the freeze now — it is justified by the payment record regardless of the news — while confirming the underlying supplier report and resolving the DPD as-of date before the High Risk band itself is released externally.

The buyer would move down to Watch below 50.0, which is 25.3 points away. The news leg cannot hold the band on its own, so the realistic route down is payment: the overdue invoice cleared and days-late reverting toward the earlier 9 and 19 day pattern, with total outstanding brought back inside the 3.0M limit. Confirmation that the supplier arrears and the overdue invoice are one event rather than two, or a failure to corroborate ILL-003, would also reduce the weight the band currently rests on. Absent that, news decay is slow at a 365-day half-life.

judgement.bottom_line: Freeze the 3000000 USD limit on LIM-OS06-1 — exposure of 3.24M already exceeds it and there is nothing left to cut, against a score of 75.3 (High Risk, PD 0.775). The adjudicator agreed with caveats: payment alone is 48.1 weighted and does not reach the band, so the High Risk label depends on a single anonymously sourced article that may be describing the same cash-flow event as the overdue invoice.
judgement.payment_note: One open overdue of USD 640,000 at 52 days past due under TCI-EX-2026-0001, on a clearly deteriorating trend of 9 then 19 then 52 days late, with combined outstanding of 3.24M now above the 3.0M limit.
judgement.news_note: A single severity 4 item (ILL-003, 15 days old) reports Hessler has fallen behind with several component suppliers after a customer postponed acceptance of two production lines, but it is second-hand from three unnamed suppliers and uncorroborated.
lifts_it: Score falling 25.3 points to below 50.0 would move the buyer to Watch
The USD 640,000 overdue cleared and days-late reverting toward the earlier 9 to 19 day pattern
Total outstanding brought back within the 3.0M limit on TCI-EX-2026-0001
worsens_it: No higher band exists above High Risk, so watch for severity rather than reband
DPD rising beyond 52 — the as-of date is unresolved, so current days late may already exceed it
Corroboration of ILL-003, or a second independent news item, which would remove the adjudicator's caveats
